How the water-heater simulator works

This page documents the actual current implementation: a full storage tank, gas or electric heating, and an ideal tap mixer that combines tank-top water with the cold supply. It is an educational numerical model, not an appliance-sizing or safety tool.

Controls

Using the page

Choose your settings, open the tap, and press Start to draw mixed water. Adjust the target temperature and total flow, then watch the tank layers cool. Close the tap to see heating restore stored energy. Compare gas and electric recovery at different powers.

ControlCurrent range / defaultWhat it changes
Litre / US gallonLitre initiallyConverts volumes and flow units. The selected flow is rounded and clamped to a valid 0.5-unit step; this can change actual flow.
°C / °F°C initiallyConverts displayed readings. The thermostat switches to whole degrees in the selected unit, rounding its setting; stored tank temperatures are unchanged.
Simulation speedSlider: 1× to 100× in steps of 1; default 10×Changes simulated time per animation frame.
Pause / ResumePaused initially; press StartStops or resumes thermal updates, elapsed time, water accumulation and particle motion. Controls still work while paused.
Start overActionSets all layers to the current thermostat setting, zeros elapsed time and tank draw, closes the tap, sets heating off and waits paused. Keeps the selected controls and units.
Open / Close hot tapClosed initiallyEnables or stops total mixed output. Heating can continue with the tap closed.
Total tap flow0.5–17 L/min, or 0.5–4.5 US gal/min; 0.5-unit steps; initial 8 L/minCombined hot-side tank flow plus cold bypass flow, not tank flow alone.
Target output temperature1–65°C (33.8–149°F); initial 40°C (104°F)Requests a blend. Actual output is restricted to the available supply temperatures.
Inlet temperature1–30°C (33.8–86°F); initial 15°C (59°F)Affects replacement water and the cold bypass immediately; does not reset stored tank temperatures.
Storage tank size50–400 L in 10 L steps; default 190 L (about 50.2 US gal)Changes layer volume and heat capacity. Restarts all layers at the thermostat setting, clears time and draw, closes the tap and pauses. Gallon mode displays converted capacity; size steps remain 10 L (about 2.64 US gal).
Thermostat40–65°C (104–149°F); initial 55°C (131°F)Uses 1°C or 1°F steps in the selected unit. Sets the lower-tank sensor's heating thresholds, not a hard cap on top-water temperature.
Heat sourceGas initially; gas or electricChanges useful power, spatial heat distribution and the diagram. Does not reset temperatures.
Gas input10,000–80,000 BTU/h, steps of 1,000; default 40,000Fuel input, with 80% assumed to reach the water.
Electric power1–12 kW, steps of 0.5; default 4.5Resistance heating, with all specified power assumed to reach the water.

The thermostat advances by 1°C in Celsius mode or 1°F in Fahrenheit mode. Its selected-unit value is converted to Celsius for physics. Inlet and target-output sliders still advance by 1°C internally (1.8°F when displayed in Fahrenheit). Reloading the page restores initial defaults; settings are not saved between reloads.

Diagram & readings

Reading the diagram

The left inlet feeds a dip tube to the bottom. Water drawn from the top joins a separate cold-supply bypass at the tap. The gas flue is a separate exhaust path, not a water pipe. Electric mode hides the gas burner and flue and shows one lower element.

The colored tank contains 24 simulated layers. Eight labels sample indices 23, 20, 17, 14, 10, 7, 4, 0, from top to bottom; they are individual readings, not eight independent tanks. “From tank” is the top-layer temperature. “Mixed output” is the calculated blend. Tank and cold branch flows appear beneath the diagram’s tank-water percentage. The sensor callout shows (T₄ + T₅)/2, the same lower-tank reading used by the thermostat. “Tank average” appears in the diagram and is the mean of all 24 layers. “Drawn from tank” is accumulated tank-side volume only and excludes cold bypass water.

With the tap closed, mixed temperature and tank-water percentage are previews; both displayed branch flows are zero. Percentage is rounded to a whole number. Accumulated tank volume rounds to whole litres or one decimal US gallon; branch flows use two decimals.

The tank stays full. Every litre drawn from it is replaced by one litre through the dip tube. White moving dashes indicate active paths; their speed is decorative, not a calibrated velocity. The browser's reduced-motion preference hides the flow dashes without pausing the physics.

z=clamp⁡(T/80,0,1)R=round⁡(81+174z)G=round⁡(184−51z)B=round⁡(255−163z)\begin{aligned}z&=\operatorname{clamp}(T/80,0,1)\\R&=\operatorname{round}(81+174z)\\G&=\operatorname{round}(184-51z)\\B&=\operatorname{round}(255-163z)\end{aligned}zRGB​=clamp(T/80,0,1)=round(81+174z)=round(184−51z)=round(255−163z)​

Temperature color uses Celsius and a fixed 0–80°C (32–176°F) scale. Colors saturate outside that interval; the temperature itself is not capped.

Temperature history

Live temperature history

The chart beneath the diagram plots tank average (solid orange) and thermostat sensor temperature (dashed blue) against simulated elapsed minutes. Tank draw rate is the tank-side flow at that time, excluding cold bypass water; a green line uses the right axis in L/min or US gal/min. The legends sit to the right. Hover over a legend item to emphasize its line and dim the others. Click a legend item to pin or unpin its highlight; multiple lines can be selected within either line chart. Pinned selections stay active while another legend item is hovered. “Reset highlights” clears selections in both charts without changing simulation time or recorded history. Keyboard focus and Enter/Space support the same interaction. All lines extend while running and stop when paused. The endpoint follows the current frame; retained history is sampled every 5 simulated seconds. Start over or changing tank size clears the history and returns it to the initial reading.

All history charts share a horizontal axis that starts at 0–10 minutes and expands by 10-minute blocks (0–20, 0–30, and so on) as simulated time exceeds the current range. One combined chart below the average/sensor chart shows eight colored lines for the diagram’s sampled sections, labeled from top to bottom (layer indices 23, 20, 17, 14, 10, 7, 4, 0). Both charts use the same sampling, reset, pause and unit-conversion behavior, with a shared vertical range for comparison. Hover over either chart to see the nearest recorded time as MM:SS and a tooltip that follows above the cursor, with a table of colored series names and values in the selected units; a vertical guide and dots mark that sample. The vertical axis starts at 0–80°C and expands if readings exceed that range; Fahrenheit mode converts the entire stored history. The diagram color scale remains fixed at 0–80°C. An additional section temperature matrix below the combined section chart has eight compact rows ordered Section 1 through Section 8, labeled on the right with the temperature scale at the bottom right. Each retained time interval is colored using its starting sample’s temperature and the diagram’s fixed 0–80°C scale. A white line within each row traces the same section temperature on a fixed 0–80°C vertical scale; values outside this range saturate at its ends. Future time stays blank. Hover within recorded time to see the nearest sample’s MM:SS time and all eight section temperatures in a color-coded table. The time axes of all three graphs align, with identical plot margins and tick positions. The matrix uses the same retained samples, pause, reset, time range, and unit conversion as the line charts. History is stored only in memory. After 12,000 retained samples, alternate samples are removed and the sampling interval doubles, retaining the full time span at lower resolution.

Tank model

State, constants and boundaries

Indices increase upward: i = 0 is the bottom and i = 23 is the top. Internally, temperatures use °C, time uses seconds, volume uses litres, and power uses kW = kJ/s.

N=24,Vtank=selected sizeVlayer=Vtank/Nρ=1  kg/Lcp=4.186  kJ/(kg⋅∘C)Clayer=ρVlayercp=33.13917  kJ/∘Cat 190  L\begin{aligned}N&=24,\quad V_{\rm tank}=\text{selected size}\\V_{\rm layer}&=V_{\rm tank}/N\\\rho&=1\;\mathrm{kg/L}\\c_p&=4.186\;\mathrm{kJ/(kg\cdot{}^{\circ}C)}\\C_{\rm layer}&=\rho V_{\rm layer}c_p\\&=33.13917\;\mathrm{kJ/{}^{\circ}C}\quad\text{at }190\;\mathrm L\end{aligned}NVlayer​ρcp​Clayer​​=24,Vtank​=selected size=Vtank​/N=1kg/L=4.186kJ/(kg⋅∘C)=ρVlayer​cp​=33.13917kJ/∘Cat 190L​

Every layer starts at 55°C. The initial thermostat is also 55°C and heating is off. The environment is fixed at 20°C. Only the bottom layer receives inlet water directly; each higher layer receives water from the layer below. Neighbor mixing has no outside neighbor at the top or bottom. All layers have equal mass, with constant density and specific heat capacity. Changing tank size changes all layer masses. It is a reset to a different hypothetical tank, not a physical filling or draining process. The diagram’s geometry stays fixed. Mixing coefficients and heat-distribution weights do not scale with size; heating and flow increments do scale through layer volume.

Relevant source: initial state, N, V, cp, step(dt), and render().

Tap mixing

Mixing cold supply with tank-top water

Let Th be top-layer temperature, Tc inlet temperature, Tr requested output, and f the tank-water fraction. Conservation of sensible heat for equal-density water gives:

Tout=fTh+(1−f)Tcf=clamp⁡(Tr−TcTh−Tc,0,1)\begin{aligned}T_{\rm out}&=fT_h+(1-f)T_c\\f&=\operatorname{clamp}\left(\frac{T_r-T_c}{T_h-T_c},0,1\right)\end{aligned}Tout​f​=fTh​+(1−f)Tc​=clamp(Th​−Tc​Tr​−Tc​​,0,1)​

The clamp limits f to 0–1. Output cannot exceed the warmer source or fall below the cooler source. The formula also works if the nominal cold supply is warmer than the tank. If |Th − Tc| < 10−8°C, the code uses f = 0 to avoid division by zero and supplies bypass water only.

Qtank=fQtapQbypass=(1−f)Qtapq=Qtank/60[L/s]Dnew=Dold+qΔt\begin{aligned}Q_{\rm tank}&=fQ_{\rm tap}\\Q_{\rm bypass}&=(1-f)Q_{\rm tap}\\q&=Q_{\rm tank}/60\quad[\mathrm{L/s}]\\D_{\rm new}&=D_{\rm old}+q\Delta t\end{aligned}Qtank​Qbypass​qDnew​​=fQtap​=(1−f)Qtap​=Qtank​/60[L/s]=Dold​+qΔt​

Q uses L/min. When the tap is closed, q = 0 and neither branch flows. The fraction is recalculated at every thermal substep as the tank changes. Lower requested temperatures generally reduce tank draw at the same total tap flow. Status text flags an unavailable target only when it is more than 0.05°C outside the source-temperature interval; the actual blend is always clamped.

Relevant source: mixture(), flowLitres(), and step(dt).

Heating & thermostat

Heating power and thermostat

Pgas=IBTU/h×0.00029307107×0.8Pelectric=selected electric kW\begin{aligned}P_{\rm gas}&=I_{\rm BTU/h}\times0.00029307107\times0.8\\P_{\rm electric}&=\text{selected electric kW}\end{aligned}Pgas​Pelectric​​=IBTU/h​×0.00029307107×0.8=selected electric kW​

These are useful water-heating powers. The gas efficiency is a fixed assumption, not a tested rating. The model neither computes fuel consumption totals nor simulates ignition, exhaust temperature or heat-pump performance.

Sensor and hysteresis

Ts=T4+T52bnew={1Ts<Tset−5∘C0Ts≥Tsetboldotherwise\begin{aligned}T_s&=\frac{T_4+T_5}{2}\\b_{\rm new}&=\begin{cases}1&T_s<T_{\rm set}-5^{\circ}\mathrm C\\0&T_s\ge T_{\rm set}\\b_{\rm old}&\text{otherwise}\end{cases}\end{aligned}Ts​bnew​​=2T4​+T5​​=⎩⎨⎧​10bold​​Ts​<Tset​−5∘CTs​≥Tset​otherwise​​

b is the heating state, evaluated at the start of each substep. The 5°C band equals 9°F. At exactly the lower threshold the state is retained. A newly changed setting takes effect in the next thermal step; when paused, no thermostat step occurs. Thermostat control is always enabled.

Where heat enters

wigas={0.110≤i≤30.0284≤i≤23wielectric={0.250≤i≤304≤i≤23∑i=023wi=1\begin{aligned}w_i^{\rm gas}&=\begin{cases}0.11&0\le i\le3\\0.028&4\le i\le23\end{cases}\\w_i^{\rm electric}&=\begin{cases}0.25&0\le i\le3\\0&4\le i\le23\end{cases}\\\sum_{i=0}^{23}w_i&=1\end{aligned}wigas​wielectric​i=0∑23​wi​​={0.110.028​0≤i≤34≤i≤23​={0.250​0≤i≤34≤i≤23​=1​

Gas delivers 44% of useful heat into the bottom four layers and 56% along the remaining layers. Electric delivers all heat into the bottom four. These weights approximate spatial heating and do not solve a heat exchanger. The lower sensor can remain cool while the top is already hotter than the setpoint, so top-water overshoot is possible.

Relevant source: power() and step(dt).

Temperature equations

Temperature update equations

Each substep first copies all temperatures into an old-state array. The following four increments are computed using that same old state, then added together for each layer. This is an explicit Euler update.

1. Flow through the tank

Tu,i={Tinleti=0Ti−1i>0ΔTflow,i=qΔtVlayer(Tu,i−Ti)\begin{aligned}T_{u,i}&=\begin{cases}T_{\rm inlet}&i=0\\T_{i-1}&i>0\end{cases}\\\Delta T_{{\rm flow},i}&=\frac{q\Delta t}{V_{\rm layer}}(T_{u,i}-T_i)\end{aligned}Tu,i​ΔTflow,i​​={Tinlet​Ti−1​​i=0i>0​=Vlayer​qΔt​(Tu,i​−Ti​)​

This models replacement and upward transport through equal, internally mixed cells. It produces numerical spreading of a temperature front rather than perfectly sharp displacement.

2. Neighbor mixing

ΔTmix,i=0.006Δt (Li+Ui)Li={Ti−1−Tii>00i=0Ui={Ti+1−Tii<230i=23\begin{aligned}\Delta T_{{\rm mix},i}&=0.006\Delta t\,(L_i+U_i)\\L_i&=\begin{cases}T_{i-1}-T_i&i>0\\0&i=0\end{cases}\\U_i&=\begin{cases}T_{i+1}-T_i&i<23\\0&i=23\end{cases}\end{aligned}ΔTmix,i​Li​Ui​​=0.006Δt(Li​+Ui​)={Ti−1​−Ti​0​i>0i=0​={Ti+1​−Ti​0​i<23i=23​​

The coefficient is 0.006 s−1. Missing neighbor terms are zero. Interior exchange is symmetric and conserves the sum of layer temperatures. This is a chosen mixing coefficient, not a measured conductivity.

3. Ambient exchange

ΔTambient,i=3×10−6Δt (20−Ti)\Delta T_{{\rm ambient},i}=3\times10^{-6}\Delta t\,(20-T_i)ΔTambient,i​=3×10−6Δt(20−Ti​)

The coefficient is 3 × 10−6 s−1. Water above 20°C loses heat; water below 20°C gains heat. The isolated continuous-time analogue is T(t) = 20 + [T(0) − 20] exp(−0.000003t), with a time constant of about 92.6 hours. The actual code uses the Euler increment above.

4. Applied heating

ΔTheat,i=bPwiΔtρVlayercpTi∗=Ti+ΔTflow,i+ΔTmix,i+ΔTambient,i+ΔTheat,i\begin{aligned}\Delta T_{{\rm heat},i}&=\frac{bPw_i\Delta t}{\rho V_{\rm layer}c_p}\\T_i^*&=T_i+\Delta T_{{\rm flow},i}+\Delta T_{{\rm mix},i}\\&\quad+\Delta T_{{\rm ambient},i}+\Delta T_{{\rm heat},i}\end{aligned}ΔTheat,i​Ti∗​​=ρVlayer​cp​bPwi​Δt​=Ti​+ΔTflow,i​+ΔTmix,i​+ΔTambient,i​+ΔTheat,i​​

Power times time is energy in kJ. Dividing by a layer's heat capacity gives a temperature increase in °C. The implementation omits explicit ρ because its assumed value is 1 kg/L.

5. Buoyancy relaxation

After those increments, the code makes exactly 24 bottom-to-top passes through adjacent pairs. Whenever a lower layer is warmer than the layer above it, it replaces both with their mean:

Ti∗>Ti+1∗⟹m=Ti∗+Ti+1∗2Ti∗←m,Ti+1∗←m\begin{aligned}T_i^*>T_{i+1}^*\quad&\Longrightarrow\quad m=\frac{T_i^*+T_{i+1}^*}{2}\\T_i^*&\leftarrow m,\qquad T_{i+1}^*\leftarrow m\end{aligned}Ti∗​>Ti+1∗​Ti∗​​⟹m=2Ti∗​+Ti+1∗​​←m,Ti+1∗​←m​

Updates within a pass are sequential. Pair averaging conserves energy for equal-mass cells and approximates warm water rising. It is not a fluid-dynamics calculation. A finite 24 passes does not guarantee a perfectly monotonic temperature profile or convergence; small inversions may remain.

Energy accounting

E=ρVlayercp∑i=023TiΔE=ρcpqΔt(Tinlet−T23)+ρVlayercp(3×10−6)Δt∑i=023(20−Ti)+bPΔt\begin{aligned}E&=\rho V_{\rm layer}c_p\sum_{i=0}^{23}T_i\\\Delta E&=\rho c_pq\Delta t(T_{\rm inlet}-T_{23})\\&\quad+\rho V_{\rm layer}c_p(3\times10^{-6})\Delta t\sum_{i=0}^{23}(20-T_i)\\&\quad+bP\Delta t\end{aligned}EΔE​=ρVlayer​cp​i=0∑23​Ti​=ρcp​qΔt(Tinlet​−T23​)+ρVlayer​cp​(3×10−6)Δti=0∑23​(20−Ti​)+bPΔt​

Old-state temperatures apply in this balance. Neighbor exchange cancels in the sum; pairwise buoyancy averaging preserves it, apart from floating-point rounding. These relationships describe one substep, not an exact continuous solution.

Time & units

Time integration and unit conversions

Δtframe=min⁡(Δtreal,0.2  s) sspeedΔt=min⁡(0.5  s,remaining frame time)\begin{aligned}\Delta t_{\rm frame}&=\min(\Delta t_{\rm real},0.2\;\mathrm s)\,s_{\rm speed}\\\Delta t&=\min(0.5\;\mathrm s,\text{remaining frame time})\end{aligned}Δtframe​Δt​=min(Δtreal​,0.2s)sspeed​=min(0.5s,remaining frame time)​

The first frame advances zero time. Each subsequent running frame is split into substeps no larger than 0.5 simulated seconds. Browser stalls longer than 0.2 seconds are discarded, so the simulated clock can lag the nominal speed when a tab is inactive or rendering is slow. Pause skips all steps. Particle dash offset changes by 42 units per real second and is independent of the selected simulation speed.

At the largest supported flow, 4.5 US gal/min ≈ 17.0344 L/min, a 0.5-second step replaces at most about 6.8% of a cell at the smallest 50 L tank (about 1.8% at 190 L). This keeps the transport increment small; it is not a general accuracy guarantee.

TF=95TC+32VUS gal=VL3.785411784QL/min=vslider{3.785411784gallon mode1litre mode\begin{aligned}T_F&=\frac95T_C+32\\V_{\rm US\,gal}&=\frac{V_{\rm L}}{3.785411784}\\Q_{\rm L/min}&=v_{\rm slider}\begin{cases}3.785411784&\text{gallon mode}\\1&\text{litre mode}\end{cases}\end{aligned}TF​VUSgal​QL/min​​=59​TC​+32=3.785411784VL​​=vslider​{3.7854117841​gallon modelitre mode​​

Temperature conversion leaves stored water temperatures unchanged. The thermostat setting converts and rounds to a whole degree in the new unit, clamped to 40–65°C or 104–149°F. For example, 132°F converts to 55.56°C and rounds to 56°C. That rounding can change subsequent heating. The sensor hysteresis remains 5°C (9°F), independent of the slider step. Flow switching also changes a control value: it converts the previous L/min to the new unit, rounds with round(value × 2) / 2, then clamps to the new range. For example, 8 L/min becomes 2.0 US gal/min (7.5708 L/min); switching back gives 7.5 L/min, not 8. Tank capacity and accumulated volume are only converted for display.

Relevant source: frame(), fmt(), volume(), and changeVolumeUnit().

Worked examples

Calculating mixing and heating

Default tap blend

With tank top at 55°C, inlet at 15°C, target 40°C and total flow 8 L/min:

f=40−1555−15=0.625Qtank=5  L/min,Qbypass=3  L/minTout=0.625(55)+0.375(15)=40∘C=104∘F\begin{aligned}f&=\frac{40-15}{55-15}=0.625\\Q_{\rm tank}&=5\;\mathrm{L/min},\quad Q_{\rm bypass}=3\;\mathrm{L/min}\\T_{\rm out}&=0.625(55)+0.375(15)\\&=40^{\circ}\mathrm C=104^{\circ}\mathrm F\end{aligned}fQtank​Tout​​=55−1540−15​=0.625=5L/min,Qbypass​=3L/min=0.625(55)+0.375(15)=40∘C=104∘F​

The diagram rounds the tank fraction to 63%. If the sources stayed constant for a minute, tank draw would be 5 L. In the running model the fraction changes as the tank cools.

A target the tank cannot supply

With tank top 35°C, inlet 15°C, and target 40°C, the raw fraction is 1.25 and clamps to 1. Actual output is 35°C. All tap flow comes from the tank. Mixing cannot create additional heat.

Default gas power and ideal recovery

P=40000(0.00029307107)(0.8)=9.37827424  kWE=190(4.186)(40)=31813.6  kJtgas=E/P≈3392.3  s≈56.5  mintelectric=E/4.5≈7069.7  s≈117.8  min\begin{aligned}P&=40000(0.00029307107)(0.8)\\&=9.37827424\;\mathrm{kW}\\E&=190(4.186)(40)=31813.6\;\mathrm{kJ}\\t_{\rm gas}&=E/P\approx3392.3\;\mathrm s\approx56.5\;\mathrm{min}\\t_{\rm electric}&=E/4.5\approx7069.7\;\mathrm s\approx117.8\;\mathrm{min}\end{aligned}PEtgas​telectric​​=40000(0.00029307107)(0.8)=9.37827424kW=190(4.186)(40)=31813.6kJ=E/P≈3392.3s≈56.5min=E/4.5≈7069.7s≈117.8min​

These are energy-only benchmarks with no draw, no losses and continuous heating. They are not simulated recovery guarantees: the actual thermostat, stratification and heat distribution alter the trajectory. These examples use the default 190 L capacity. Ideal energy and recovery time scale with tank volume. The simulator begins hot and paused, not at 15°C.

Average temperature and useful heat

Tavg=124∑i=023TidTavgdt∣heating=PρVtankcp\begin{aligned}T_{\rm avg}&=\frac1{24}\sum_{i=0}^{23}T_i\\\left.\frac{dT_{\rm avg}}{dt}\right|_{\rm heating}&=\frac{P}{\rho V_{\rm tank}c_p}\end{aligned}Tavg​dtdTavg​​​heating​​=241​i=0∑23​Ti​=ρVtank​cp​P​​

For the default 190 L tank, at default gas power this is about 0.7075°C per minute, before ambient loss and draw. At 4.5 kW it is about 0.3395°C per minute.

Limitations

What this model does not predict

  • Water pressure, pipe travel time, pump behavior, hydraulic resistance, expansion, relief valves, boiling, or evaporation.
  • Actual gas combustion, flue heat transfer, ignition delays, realistic two-element electric controls, or manufacturer-specific efficiency.
  • A calibrated thermal front, three-dimensional circulation, sediment, inlet jets, detailed insulation, or temperature-dependent density and heat capacity.
  • Real mixing-valve response time: the ideal valve adjusts instantly and has no flow limit or control lag.
  • A hard maximum outlet temperature. The thermostat senses lower layers; the top can exceed its setting and the color scale.
  • Exact wall-clock acceleration when browser frames are delayed. Animation speed and line thickness do not measure flow.

Changing settings while paused updates previews, but thermal evolution waits for Resume. The visible heating state can therefore still reflect the last thermal step. Closing the tap stops draw, not heating. Start over deliberately creates a uniformly hot initial tank rather than modeling a refill or reheating cycle.

Updating this README

Keeping this README current

Invoke $water-heater-readme to review the current build and update this page. The skill rereads implementation and controls, recalculates examples, updates formulas and limitations, and refreshes the reviewed build fingerprint. It does not automatically run when the simulation is edited.

The former “About this model” panel is incorporated into the tank model, heating, mixing and limitations sections above. The simulator is self-contained in dist/index.html; this README is dist/readme.html. Both work offline. Formulas are authored in LaTeX and pre-rendered with bundled KaTeX 0.16.22; local fonts and CSS require no network connection. Opening the simulator initializes its animation loop but leaves physics paused until Start. Optional browser agent integration registers configure_water_heater when supported, allowing tap and pause state to be set and returning mixed and tank-top temperatures; it is not required for ordinary use.
